land.text: the Thracian plain between 'Philippi (or Philippopolis)' (Plovdiv) and 'Arcadiopolis' (Luleburgaz), where Strabo 'at the command of his people in Thrace' operated and died 'near Philippi in Thrace': Plovdiv, Stara Zagora and Haskovo (Bulgaria), Edirne and Kirklareli (Turkey), without Constantinople

predecessors.note: Thrace was Eastern Roman land: 'In 471, the Alan Aspar ... was murdered by order of the emperor himself. Strabo, who was at the command of his people in Thrace, revolted to avenge his relative.' The Goths already lived in Thrace; the revolt turns them into a rival power, so the hand-over is nominal.

successors.note: The land was never held by the Goths alone and stays Eastern Roman. Strabo died in 481 and the dossier ends there. The Ostrogoths page: 'His son Recitac was unable to retain Gothic support and was killed in 484 under orders from Theoderic the Amal, who united the two Gothic groups', while the Zeno page has Theoderic the Amal king 'of the entire Ostrogoth nation' after Strabo's death in 481; no page gives Recitach any land or a relation with Rome, so 481-484 is not drawn. The followers joined the Amal's Goths (ostrogoths dossier), who left for Italy in 488.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 471-481: the Goths of Theodoric Strabo in Thrace, redrawn 2026-10-24 after review. The page places Strabo 'at the command of his people in Thrace' in 471, has part of the army attack 'Philippi (or Philippopolis)' and 'led the remaining men to attack and occupy Arcadiopolis', and has him die in 481 'during an encampment at Stabulum Diomedis, near Philippi in Thrace'; in 480/481 he 'moved towards Constantinople' (the page does not say the Goths held, attacked or besieged the city). The first draft was the whole region of Thrace (287 cells, about 72,600 km2), which includes Constantinople: the Eastern capital was drawn as contested in 471-473 and 474-481 and as the Goths' sole land in 473-474 and 481-484. The new shape is the Thracian plain between the two named cities: admin1 Plovdiv, Stara Zagora, Haskovo, Edirne and Kirklareli, 92 cells, about 23,300 km2, without Istanbul (gazetteer 2026-10-24); it overlaps eastern-roman-empire_469/490 (90 cells, as it must: the land is contested or federate throughout) and no Ostrogothic shape. Land and relation to Rome in each period: 471-473 contested (contest 471/473), 473-474 federate (peace with Leo: 'the Byzantines were to pay an annual tribute of 2000 pounds of gold to the Goths' and 'Strabo was to obtain the rank of magister militum'; drawn as the batch's federate tint, a reading), January 474-481 contested again (contest 474/481), so the Goths are never the sole holders of Eastern Roman land. The Ostrogoths page adds that 'For some time they held a part of Macedonia, controlling part of the Via Egnatia', but the sentence's subject is unclear and the strip is not drawn. The Goths did not hold all of the plain; soft. Infobox area: none on the page.

ledger.note: 471: Theodoric Strabo revolts in Thrace. 'In 471, the Alan Aspar, at the time magister militum of Emperor Leo I, was murdered by order of the emperor himself. Strabo, who was at the command of his people in Thrace, revolted to avenge his relative.' The Ostrogoths page dates the revolt to 473 and says he 'was declared king of the Goths'; the page's own 473 is the peace. He sought Aspar's properties and the right to settle his Goths in Thrace.

ledger.note: 471: Strabo's Goths attack Philippopolis and take Arcadiopolis. Strabo attacked 'Philippi (or Philippopolis)' and took 'Arcadiopolis'; Leo refused his demands. Philippopolis is Plovdiv; the page does not date the two cities separately from the revolt. Philippopolis is Plovdiv and Arcadiopolis is Luleburgaz in Kirklareli province; the region is the plain between them.

ledger.note: 473: peace with Leo. 'When the Goths ran out of supplies, Strabo signed a peace with Leo (473)'; the Goths' 'independence was recognized' and the Byzantines paid an annual tribute. The page does not say land was granted. The contest closes here and the federate relation (next event) opens.

ledger.note: 473: peace with Leo; the Goths become Roman federates. 'When the Goths ran out of supplies, Strabo signed a peace with Leo (473)'; 'according to its terms the Byzantines were to pay an annual tribute of 2000 pounds of gold to the Goths' and 'Strabo was to obtain the rank of magister militum'. The page grants no land. Drawn as the batch's federate tint with the empire as counterpart (the heruli and gothic-foederati dossiers do the same); the page says the tribute flowed to the Goths, so the vassal reading is the author's (confidence 2).

ledger.note: January 474 onward: Strabo rebels against Zeno. 'At the death of Leo (January 474), Strabo rebelled against the newly appointed Emperor Zeno'; he 'killed Heraclius, the magister militum per Thracias, despite the payment of a ransom', backed Basiliscus in 475, and did not defend Basiliscus in 476. The Zeno page: 'At the death of Leo II, Theodoric Strabo rebelled against Zeno.' In 476/477 Zeno 'allied himself with Strabo's rival, Theodoric the Amal'.

ledger.note: 481: Strabo dies. 'Strabo defeated the Bulgars in 480/481, and moved towards Constantinople, but he had to deal with problems with his own men', and died in 481 'during an encampment at Stabulum Diomedis, near Philippi in Thrace' (the Ostrogoths page: 'Between 479 and 481, it was the Thracian Goths under Theoderic Strabo who kept the Romans occupied, but in 481 Strabo died'). The page gives no treaty; the war lapses with his death, and his son Recitach carries on to 484. The Goths' extent after 481 is not given by any page opened.

ledger.note: 481: Strabo dies and the Thracian Goths' war ends. He died in 481 'during an encampment at Stabulum Diomedis, near Philippi in Thrace'. The dossier used to run to 484 (Recitach killed, Ostrogoths page: 'killed in 484 under orders from Theoderic the Amal, who united the two Gothic groups'); the Zeno page has Theoderic the Amal king 'of the entire Ostrogoth nation' after 481. No page gives Recitach land or a relation with Rome, so the polity is closed at Strabo's death (review of 2026-10-24: land not drawn twice). The followers pass to the ostrogoths dossier; the Thracian land stays Roman.

wars.outcome: Strabo rebels against Zeno in 474, backs Basiliscus in 475, is attacked by Theoderic the Amal on Zeno's order in 476/477-478, and dies in 481 after defeating the Bulgars; no treaty ends the war.
wars.note: An agreement with Zeno (money to pay 13,000 soldiers, the title magister militum back) is on the Zeno page without a year; the Strabo page puts the Amal's attack in 478 and a joint request by both Theoderics 'to extend to the south the settlement territory of the Goths in Moesia'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Goths are placed 'in Thrace' and by three place names (Philippopolis, Arcadiopolis, Stabulum Diomedis near Philippi). The shape is the plain between the first two.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-d ('Theoderic Strabo's Goths (Thracian Goths)', 473-481). Four pages opened. The pages disagree on the revolt (471 on the Strabo page, 473 on the Ostrogoths page) and give no extent for the Goths' land; Thrace is the page's only place name for the people, and the shape is soft (ten years held at most as a warband in a Roman province). The first draft ran to 484 (Recitach killed, Ostrogoths page); it now ends in 481 (Strabo's death). The Strabo page places the Goths before 471 'in Getea and Peuce island in the Danube delta' (citation needed) and the Ostrogoths page has the Amal's Goths in Moesia; the ostrogoths dossier covers the Amal group. No capital is named. Gazetteer: Philippopolis and Arcadiopolis (Luleburgaz) are only used in text. Wikidata id unknown. Repair of 2026-10-24 (review eu-06-x): (1) {region: Thrace} (287 cells) contained Constantinople and Edirne; the page never has the Goths holding the city, so the shape is now the plain between Philippopolis and Arcadiopolis (Plovdiv, Stara Zagora, Haskovo, Edirne, Kirklareli; 92 cells). (2) The Goths were drawn as sole holders of land that eastern-roman-empire_469 also holds (269 of 287 cells); 473-474 is now a federate interval (vassal_start/vassal_end with eastern-roman-empire, month 1 of 474 for the end) and the dossier ends in 481, so 473-474 and 481-484 no longer double-draw the land. Not changed: Recitach's 481-484 is undrawn; the Ostrogoths page (484) and the Zeno page (union after 481) disagree. Direction of the federate events: the schema describes vassal_start's counterpart as the vassal itself, whereas this batch (heruli, gothic-foederati, thracian-goths) records the federate's tie with the suzerain as counterpart; the orchestrator should settle which reading the renderer uses. Requests: eastern-roman-empire (eu-05-a) needs contests with thracian-goths 471-473 and 474-481 and the 473-474 vassal pair; ostrogoths should record the followers' union (481/484).
